analysis: Reviewed the single changed unit, a test-only file (provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Autopilot/AutopilotBusyReasonTests.swift). The PR adds an `addon_hold` busy reason to the stable wire-vocabulary assertion (line 17) and adds raise/lower test helpers for `.addonHold` (lines 218-220, 247-249) that insert/end an AddonHold and begin/resume the serving drain. No production code is changed in this unit, so no auth, attestation, encryption, data exposure or billing behavior changes here. The changed test only pins the ordering and spelling of the busy-reason wire vocabulary and exercises state toggling in the test fixture. Threat-model relevance is limited: the production addon-hold and servingDrain machinery, and the `addon_hold` reason surfaced in the modelAutopilot snapshot (a provider-to-coordinator status field), are outside the supplied evidence. The next review pass should check the production source for the AddonHold type, ServingDrain.begin(.addonHold)/resumeAddonHold, and ModelAutopilotBusyReason. Points to verify: the hold lease is bounded, so a hold cannot indefinitely stall serving (DoS, T-057-like availability); the new busy reason exposes no sensitive detail; and hold release is reliable. None of that can be judged from this test file. No regression identified in the supplied unit.
